Consult Summary:
- 19-year-old female with 3 days of dysuria and lower abdominal cramping; clinician suspects uncomplicated urinary tract infection and plans a short course of oral antibiotics plus supportive measures and safety-net follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Painful urination (stinging/burning) for a few days.
  - Lower abdominal crampy pain associated with urination.
  - Small amount of visible blood in urine earlier today.
  - Urine noted to have an unusual smell.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms started a few days ago; described as not severe but bothersome; no documented improvement prior to visit.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - No specific exacerbating factors identified.
  - Patient tried over-the-counter bicarbonate a few days ago without improvement.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - No increased urinary frequency reported.
  - No flank or back pain.
  - No nausea or vomiting.
  - No fevers (patient initially unclear but ultimately reported no fever).
  - Bowel movements reported as normal; no diarrhea.
  - No abnormal vaginal discharge reported.
- Sexual/reproductive history:
  - Sexually active with a single boyfriend for a few months.
  - Uses condoms for contraception.
  - Never had an STD screen (patient believes she has never had one).
  - Last menstrual period: patient stated “a couple of weeks ago”; clinician later stated “three weeks ago” (conflict noted).
  - Patient believes she is unlikely to be pregnant; clinician advised pregnancy test if concern.
- Other relevant:
  - Past history of IBS (see PMH).
  - No other systemic complaints.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable bowel syndrome (patient-reported).
- Allergies:
  - Clindamycin — causes swelling (patient-reported; appears clinically significant).
- Current medications:
  - Over-the-counter bicarbonate recently tried for symptoms (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - No regular prescription medications reported.

Social History:
- Living situation:
  - Lives in a flat near college with friends.
- Occupation/education:
  - Student studying biology.
- Tobacco/alcohol/substance use:
  - Does not smoke.
  - Drinks alcohol socially on weekends.
  - No other substance use reported.
- Sexual practices:
  - Sexually active; uses condoms; advised to avoid intercourse while symptomatic.

Family History:
- No known family history of kidney, bladder, bowel, or gut disease reported.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Examination findings: not documented (clinician stated would proceed to examination but no exam findings were recorded).

Investigations:
- No investigations, urinalysis, urine culture, pregnancy test, or STI testing documented or performed during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected uncomplicated urinary tract infection (acute cystitis)
  - Assessment: Clinical impression of simple UTI based on dysuria, lower abdominal discomfort, malodorous urine, and hematuria.
  - Plan:
    - Offer antibiotic therapy: either nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim to be given as a short course.
      - Regimen discussed: one tablet orally twice daily for 3 days; specific medication dose not documented.
      - Note: medication names provided; exact dose (mg) not documented.
    - Advise increased fluid intake to help flush the urinary tract.
    - Cranberry juice may be tried for symptomatic relief.
    - Recommend avoiding sexual intercourse while symptoms persist; continue condom use if sexual activity occurs.
    - Safety-net: return or call if not improved by the end of the week or sooner if developing fever, back/flank pain, or increasing systemic illness (concern for possible ascending infection/pyelonephritis).
    - If pregnancy is a concern, perform a pregnancy test prior to or at start of treatment (clinician advised this, but no test documented).
- Issue 2: Allergy — Clindamycin
  - Assessment: Reported allergic reaction with swelling when exposed to clindamycin.
  - Plan:
    - Document allergy and avoid prescribing clindamycin.
- Issue 3: Past IBS (stable)
  - Assessment: History of irritable bowel syndrome; not currently active or queried in detail.
  - Plan:
    - No active management changes documented for IBS during this consult.

General plan items:
- If symptoms persist despite antibiotic course, re-evaluate clinically and consider further investigations (urine dipstick, urine culture, STI screen, pelvic exam, pregnancy testing) — clinician advised follow-up but no specific tests were ordered in this encounter.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (temperature, pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate) not documented.
  - Physical examination findings (abdominal, costovertebral angle, pelvic/genitourinary) not documented despite clinician stating intention to examine.
  - No urinalysis, urine dipstick, or urine culture performed or recorded.
  - No pregnancy test result recorded; clinician advised testing if concerned.
  - Specific antibiotic choice selected and exact dose (mg) not documented — only medication options and tablet frequency given.
  - No formal STI testing offered or ordered despite sexual activity and no prior screening.
  - Medication reconciliation is limited (no complete list of current medications).
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Last menstrual period timing: patient stated “a couple of weeks ago”; clinician later documented “three weeks ago” (conflict noted).
  - Patient initially said “think so” when asked about fever, then clarified “no” (minor clarity issue).
- Transcript quality:
  - Conversation contains a few instances of hesitation and brief inaudible or overlapping speech, but overall information was sufficient to extract history and plan.
